problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the coordinates of the point ${Y}^{′}$, the image of $Y(-2,-3)$ under the action of $T?$

${Y}^{′}($ 
{{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$)$
worked_solution:
To find the image of $Y$ under the action of $T$, we first create a column-vector $x$ containing the coordinates of $Y:$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $x$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $Tx:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Tx & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The result, $Tx,$ contains the coordinates of ${Y}^{′}.$ Therefore, ${Y}^{′}(-2,11).$
